precepts.text: Elias is come already, and they knew him not; the disciples understood that he spake unto them of John the Baptist.
precepts.point: The son of Zacharias was John the Baptist, a Levite; and John the Baptist was Elijah back on the earth again, come to do what was prophesied of him. There is no reincarnation, coming back as a bird or such; there is regeneration, and we come back over and over again.

note.label: Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order

precepts.why:
The son of Zacharias was John the Baptist, a Levite of that priestly line. And John the Baptist was Elijah back on the earth again, come to do what was prophesied of him. “But I say unto you, That Elias is come already, and they knew him not, but have done unto him whatsoever they listed. Likewise shall also the Son of man suffer of them. Then the disciples understood that he spake unto them of John the Baptist.”

There is no reincarnation, coming back as a bird or such; there is regeneration, and we come back over and over again. Elias came already as John the Baptist, and they knew him not.

precepts.text: Moses and Elias appeared talking with Christ on the mount; Moses is good.
precepts.point: Moses is still good; he stood with Elias before Christ on the mount. He missed the promised land at that time, not the kingdom. But leadership carries the greater condemnation: the more given unto you, the more stripes when you fail.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
“And, behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him.” Moses is still good. The judgment at the waters kept him out of the promised land at that time, but it did not keep him out of the kingdom: he stood with Elias before Christ on the mount, talking with him.

So “Thou also shalt not go in thither” was the loss of the land, not of the kingdom. But it stands as the warning for leadership, which carries the greater condemnation: the more given unto you, the more stripes when you fail, and Moses, who was given so much, missed the land for one failure at the rock.

precepts.text: A voice out of the cloud says, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him," showing Christ is the only other prophet the Most High dealt with face to face and put his words in his mouth.
precepts.point: "Like unto thee," like unto Moses, means the same similarities: Moses spoke to the Most High directly, mediated between the Most High and Israel, gave the laws, was hidden as a child when the young were sought to be killed, and led Israel toward the promised land.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
“While he yet spake, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them: and behold a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.”

Hear ye him: the same words Moses used, him shall ye hear in all things. Christ is the only other prophet the Most High dealt with face to face and put his words in his mouth.

Like unto Moses means the same similarities. Moses spoke to the Most High directly, mediated between the Most High and Israel, gave the laws, was hidden as a child when the young were sought to be killed, and led Israel toward the promised land. Christ is that prophet.

precepts.text: Moses and Elias appear, but the voice out of the cloud says this is my beloved Son, hear ye him, showing the name and authority is Christ's, not another man's.
precepts.point: You cannot sneak into the kingdom through Islam, the Nation of Islam, Jehovah's Witnesses, Mormonism, Pentecostalism, Seventh-day Adventism, the Baptists, or Buddhism. Whoever climbs up some other way is a thief and a robber trying to sneak in without laboring; you must enter by the door, which is Christ.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
On the mount “there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him”, and Peter wanted to build three tabernacles, “one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.” But the voice out of the cloud singled out one: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.”

None other name means no other power or authority was given to any man. Christians reduce it to saying the words in the name of Jesus, but the name is the authority, and that authority was given to Christ alone. There is no salvation in Moses or Elias, only through Christ.

This goes for brothers out there saying John the Baptist was wicked. John the Baptist by this time had gotten killed already, but now Christ knew his crucifixion was coming, and look what happened. Remember John is dead already.

“And after six days Jesus taketh Peter, James, and John his brother, and bringeth them up into an high mountain apart, And was transfigured before them: and his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light.” Watch this. “And, behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him.” So John the Baptist was talking to Christ with Moses. How you going to read that and go, "Oh, he was wicked"? You are stupid as hell; something's wrong with you. John got killed already, and now in the spirit realm the disciples saw Christ speaking with Moses and John the Baptist, Elijah. You can't make this stuff up.

points: This kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting: there are levels to demons, and the one that controls your mind and thoughts, like the spirit on Sarah in Tobit that killed her husbands without her knowing, is high level; why call it to yourself?

Prayer and fasting build the spiritual power of the Holy Spirit in you; when his spirit feels drained he fasts. His son had seizures at seven, he threw out the medication, fasted and prayed, and there was never another; that is his faith, not an instruction.

note.label: Restoring the Broken Minds of the Daughters of Zion

points: O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you? Depending on who is reading, you can hear the frustration in Christ's voice. Christ got frustrated, got angry, was fed up at times. Did that mean he did not love them? No. He dealt that way because it was necessary.

How many times have you told your wife what she was doing was wrong, and it became, why are you so mean? It is not me being mean; I am telling you what it is. Why can you not receive it like they received it from Christ? Many times your wife does not see Christ in you, brother, so everything is taken offensively. And we recognize, sisters, some brothers are not trying to build up, they are trying to tear down; but it is not for you to decide when. You have to put it in the Lord's hands.

How do we get out of this bashful spirit? Jesus said unto them, Because of your unbelief: for verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you. If you have faith, you will have confidence; you will speak strong; you will not be bashful.

Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting. If you have the bashful spirit, pray and fast about it. If you see your leader is lacking confidence, pray and fast for him. Has anybody tried that? The leadership did not grow up in this truth; we were all dealing with the same things, and we have to make ourselves uncomfortable and fight that spirit to be men of God.
Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting. That is the only way to get rid of certain demons: believe his word, meditate in his word, change your mind according to his word, and fast.
